title: app/render/palette.odin adds `import "core:strings"` but no added or pre-existing code references `strings` — Odin fails the build on unused imports
detail: The import is newly added (the file compiled without it before, so no pre-existing code uses it), and none of the added hunks (parse_mode_table, palette_token_by_name, palette_apply_mode, mode_class_color — which does a manual byte loop) call strings.*. Odin errors on unused imports.
recommended_fix: Delete the strings import, or replace the manual byte-compare loop in mode_class_color with a strings comparison.

title: Settings panel can open at Game_Over but is never drawn there — an invisible modal hijacks all input including the R/Enter retry
detail: draw_hud returns early on the game-over branch before the chip/panel draw, yet settings_click and the S key (mouse_map, no mode gate) still set panel_open. The modal key/mouse gates then eat Enter (→Settings_Activate) and suppress R, with zero visual feedback.
recommended_fix: Gate Toggle_Settings/settings_click on mode != .Game_Over, or draw the chip+panel before the game-over early return.

title: S is newly bound to Toggle_Settings while the QoS panel's own hint still advertises S as a lane key ("[1/2 + E/S/B]") — the diff shows no reconciliation
evidence:
+		case .S:
+			append(out, Intent(Toggle_Settings{}))
 ...and:
 			row_label = fmt.tprintf("%s -> %s  [1/2 + E/S/B]", app.cat.packet_types[i].display, lane_label(lane))
detail: poll.odin already polled E/S/B for the QoS lane surface; mouse_map now emits Toggle_Settings on S in the closed-panel branch with no sel_pipe/qos gate. If QoS lane handling still consumes the S Key_Press (e.g. in phase-2), one press both opens the panel and changes a lane.
recommended_fix: Pick one owner for S: gate the QoS lane key when the settings binding fires, or move the settings toggle to an unbound key and update hints.

title: draw_hud top-left + game-over blocks scale font sizes via hud() but leave the row y-positions unscaled — text overlaps at x1.25/x1.50
evidence:
-	draw_text(app, "Packet Plumber - v2", 12, 10, 22, p.ink)
+	draw_text(app, "Packet Plumber - v2", 12, 10, rnd.hud(&app.view, 22), p.ink)
...
+		draw_text(app, "draw pipes; P / Space pauses; U previews upgrade", 12, 36, rnd.hud(&app.view, 14), p.ink_soft)
...
+		draw_text(app, score, 12, 56, rnd.hud(&app.view, 16), p.ink_soft)
detail: At x1.50 the title is 33px tall at y=10 (bottom 43) while the hint sits at unscaled y=36 and the score at unscaled y=56 — guaranteed overlap. Same defect in the game-over block: 45px "YOU WIN" at y=68 vs retry hint at unscaled y=104.
recommended_fix: Route the y-positions (10/36/56/68/76/104) through hud() as well, or derive each row from the previous row's scaled height.

title: qos_panel.odin scaling is partial: action slot 1, preset chips, nudge rects, the proportion bar, and the weight text stay unscaled while siblings scale
detail: Slot 0 is scaled, slot 1 is not; preset-chip and nudge rect math keeps raw QOS_PANEL_X/96px constants while qos_row_y and text offsets scale. At x1.50 the panel geometry and its unscaled interior controls diverge — the exact one-surface-scaled-one-not defect.
recommended_fix: Apply hud()/hud_f() uniformly in qos_action_rect slot 1, qos_preset_chip_rect, qos_nudge_rect, the proportion-bar width, and the weight-value draw_text.

title: pulse_read is documented as "the ONE seam every animated pulse consumer routes through" but crisis.odin bypasses it with an inline gate
evidence:
+// 7.3 (E9.2): the motion-gated pulse read — the ONE seam every animated
+// pulse consumer routes through.
...
+	table := PULSE16
+	phase := (tick + u64(b)) % 16
+	factor := table[phase]
+	if v.reduced_motion {
+		factor = 1.0
+	}
detail: Behaviorally equivalent today, but the claimed single-seam invariant is false inside this very diff: the crisis outline re-implements the gate instead of calling pulse_read, inviting divergent future consumers.
recommended_fix: Either route draw_crisis_outlines through pulse_read (or a shared helper) or soften the comment to describe two sanctioned call sites.

title: Audio row claims apply+persist but A11y_Settings and the 6-byte file format have no mute field — mute is never persisted, contradicting the effect's doc comment
evidence:
+// row tapped / focused-and-activated). Rows: palette cycle (delta 0 = next,
+// ±1 = step), reduced-motion toggle, ui-scale step (±1, clamped), audio
+// mute (toggle). Every change lands in the effective view + the settings
+// file.
...
+	case rnd.SETTINGS_ROW_AUDIO:
+		au.toggle_mute(&app.audio)
+	}
+	settings_save(app.a11y)
...
+A11y_Settings :: struct {
+	palette:       rnd.Palette_Mode,
+	reduced_motion: bool,
+	scale_step:    u8, // 0..UI_SCALE_COUNT-1
+}
detail: The audio case mutates only the audio engine and then saves an unchanged struct; the format comment itself ("three u8 values") confirms mute is absent. The doc comment overpromises; a panel row labeled AUDIO silently reverts on relaunch.
recommended_fix: Either add a muted field + version the format, or correct the comments to state the audio row is session-only (as settings.odin's header implies).

title: Modal gate ordering differs across devices: controller.odin places the panel gate BEFORE the Game_Over check, touch.odin AFTER it
detail: With the panel open at Game_Over, the pad can still navigate/adjust/close the panel while touch taps are dropped entirely. Same modal, two behaviors — the per-device gates were placed inconsistently.
recommended_fix: Pick one order (recommend panel gate first on all devices, or Gate panel opening on mode) and apply it uniformly.

title: Closed-panel branch maps Up/Down to Settings_Navigate intents the executor immediately discards, while Left/Right are left unmapped — inconsistent dead emission
evidence:
+		case .Up:
+			append(out, Intent(Settings_Navigate{delta = -1}))
+		case .Down:
+			append(out, Intent(Settings_Navigate{delta = +1}))
...(closed branch) and the executor:
+	case Settings_Navigate:
+		// 7.3: move the focused row (only while open — a stray nav intent is a
+		// no-op, matching the modal gate at the mapping layer).
+		if inp.panel_open {
detail: poll.odin polls all four arrows; the closed branch emits nav intents for Up/Down that are guaranteed no-ops, and emits nothing for Left/Right. Harmless but pointless traffic, and asymmetric within the same switch.
recommended_fix: Drop the Up/Down cases from the closed branch (the panel-open gate already handles arrows) or map all four consistently.

title: input.odin comment references a non-existent symbol SETTINGS_ROWS; the constant is SETTINGS_ROW_COUNT
evidence:
+	panel_open: bool,

...
